questions.q: What mode were all of this course's earlier Auto Loader examples actually using, without naming it?
options: File notification mode using Event Grid and a queue
A mode that requires no state tracking at all
Directory listing mode — periodically listing the directory and diffing against its own state
A manual watermark-based batch pattern
questions.explain: Every earlier example ran in directory listing mode by default, without ever needing to name it at modest scale.

questions.q: Why does directory listing's cost keep growing over time even when new data per run stays small?
options: Directory listing mode is not affected by directory size at all
Listing cost scales with how many objects and prefixes exist under the path, not just how many are new
Listing mode charges a flat fee regardless of directory size
Listing cost only depends on file notification settings
questions.explain: A deep, continuously growing tree means every trigger re-lists a mostly-unchanged structure, which is a real, scaling API cost.

questions.q: What does cloudFiles.useNotifications set to true actually change?
options: It removes the need for a checkpointLocation
It converts the stream from streaming to batch processing
Auto Loader reads new-file notices from a cloud-native event queue instead of periodically listing the directory
It disables schema evolution entirely
questions.explain: File notification mode relies on cloud storage events (e.g. Event Grid + a queue) pushing notices, instead of Auto Loader listing.

questions.q: According to this lesson, when is file notification mode's setup cost actually worth paying?
options: Only when running on a single-node cluster
For very large or deep directory trees, high-frequency file arrival, or low-latency requirements
It's always worth it, even for a directory with ten files
Never — directory listing mode is always the better choice
questions.explain: Notification mode trades setup cost for eliminating re-listing cost, which pays off specifically at large scale or high arrival rate.

questions.q: What one-time setup does file notification mode require that directory listing mode never needed?
options: Permission to create a cloud event subscription and a queue (e.g. Event Grid + Queue Storage on Azure)
Manually writing the entire table schema by hand
A dedicated GPU-enabled cluster
A separate Unity Catalog metastore
questions.explain: Notification mode needs infrastructure permissions to create the event subscription and queue that listing mode doesn't require.
